description: 🚀 ¡Bienvenidos a nuestro equipo. ¡Hola a todos! Mi nombre es Santino Musacchio y soy estudiante de la Escuela Industrial N.º 9 de Argentina. Es un gusto formar parte de este concurso relacionado con la NASA, en el que vamos a trabajar en la creación de un software para monitorear el cuerpo humano en el espacio.
summary:
Our AstroSalud project is designed to comprehensively monitor the physical and mental health of astronauts during their space missions.

To this end, software has been developed that allows each astronaut to record daily measurements, track their progress through charts, and receive alerts whenever any of their values ​​fall outside established reference ranges.

Furthermore, the system includes a psychological assessment that evaluates each astronaut’s emotional and mental state based on their responses. Depending on the results, recommendations are provided to support their psychological well-being and to identify any situations that may require closer attention.

The primary objective of AstroSalud is to provide continuous, personalized monitoring for each astronaut, facilitating the early detection of potential health issues and contributing to the care of their physical and mental well-being throughout the entire mission.
details:
AstroSalud: Project description

AstroSalud records and tracks each astronaut’s health indicators: heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, body temperature, glucose, hours of sleep, mood and radiation exposure.

The data is shown on a dashboard with charts and a figure of the human body, so you can see at a glance how each astronaut is doing over time.

The program has a three-level alert system:

  • Green: values are within normal ranges.
  • Yellow: some values should be monitored.
  • Red: the situation is critical and needs immediate attention.

Depending on the level, the system shows recommendations or sends alerts to the crew and to the doctors on Earth.

It also includes a psychological assessment with questions about mood, stress and loneliness, to follow each astronaut’s emotional well-being.

Project benefits

AstroSalud tracks physical and mental health in the same system. Because values are recorded regularly and plotted on charts, changes in the indicators are caught early, which helps prevent complications on long missions. The recommendations are based on both the measurements and the answers to the psychological assessment. Medical information can be exported as a PDF and sent to the medical team on Earth.

Expected impact

AstroSalud aims to improve astronauts’ care and safety, especially on long-duration missions. On those missions, microgravity, radiation and isolation cause physical and psychological changes in the body.

Tools, programming languages and devices used

The project was developed in Visual Studio Code. The system and its graphical interface are written in C++. The medical assessment module uses FastAPI, a Python framework, to process user responses and handle the exchange of that information.

The planned setup includes the following monitoring devices:

  • Smart shirts with ECG sensors.
  • Pulse oximeters to measure oxygen saturation.
  • Activity bands or rings.
  • Body temperature sensors.
  • Glucose monitors.
  • Dosimeters to track radiation exposure.

These devices would provide data on the astronauts’ health that adds to the records entered in the software.

Project creativity

What makes AstroSalud original is that it brings physical and psychological monitoring together in one system designed for astronauts. Besides showing measurements, it organizes the information, shows how it changes over time and uses color-coded alerts so the results are quick to read.

Factors considered by the team

The team took into account the main factors that affect health during a space mission: microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation and distance from Earth, cardiovascular changes, bone and muscle loss, sleep disturbances and mental health problems.

The team also wanted the system to be easy to use without requiring too many devices for the astronaut. It also has to let astronauts enter data regularly and keep working even when communication with Earth is delayed.
